# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 94 (Bi-Vb Pc94)
**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc94
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 94
**Title (English, from literature):** Sitting in front without permission
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bi-vb-pc94
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 94 (*Anāpucchā*) establishes that a Buddhist nun commits an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) if she sits down on a seat in front of a monk without having asked for permission [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997; Bechert et al. 1997]. In the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka (Vin IV 343), there is no equivalent restriction imposed upon monks [Hüsken 1997; Bechert et al. 1997]. As Ute Hüsken observes, this rule distinctly illustrates the institutional subordination of nuns to monks, placing nuns in a position comparable to monks undergoing probation (*parivāsa*) or penance (*mānatta*) for a *saṃghādisesa* offense, who are likewise prohibited from sitting uninvited before monks in good standing [Hüsken 1997]. Hüsken further notes that this rule and the subsequent Pācittiya 95 (forbidding a nun from questioning a monk without leave) are thematically comparable to the eight strict observances (*garudhammā*) found in the Cullavagga [Hüsken 1997].
In terms of parallels, SuttaCentral curates corresponding rules in the Pali Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Bhikkhunī Parivāra (both Pācittiya 94), as well as in Chinese Sarvāstivāda Vinaya texts (Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 104) [SuttaCentral]. Secondary scholarship notes that the rule has no direct counterpart in the Mahāsāṃghika-Lokottaravāda Bhikkhunī Vinaya [Bechert et al. 1997]. According to DharmaNexus, the text exhibits extensive Pali-internal text reuse across 82 texts, sharing its most substantial matches with adjacent or related Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga rules such as Pācittiya 95 (§0.1–1.7) and Pācittiya 16 (§2.1.10–2.3.7), alongside cross-language alignments with the Sanskrit *Pravāraṇāvastu* and Tibetan *Vinayasaṃgraha* [DharmaNexus].
